title: Decide whether Copilot can use web content (web search)
problem: Security asks whether prompts can be sent to Bing for web grounding and wants a control.
steps: Review how web search works: Copilot sends short generated search queries to Bing — not the full prompt, files or Entra identity (very short prompts can be sent as-is).
Control it with the 'Allow web search in Copilot' policy in Cloud Policy service for Microsoft 365: enabled, disabled, or disabled in Work mode but enabled in Web mode and Copilot Chat.
For finer control, a Purview DLP rule can block web search only when prompts contain sensitive information types.
Document the decision and communicate it to users.

Verify: web search query logging lets you audit and eDiscover the exact queries Copilot derived from prompts. After the policy reaches clients, run a test prompt in Copilot Chat and confirm in Purview audit whether a web search query was (or was not) recorded for the test user.
pitfalls: Turning off web search reduces answer quality for public-information questions.
Policies are applied via Cloud Policy and can take time to reach clients.
The DPA and EU Data Boundary don't apply to the generated Bing queries.

Web search is not the only outside-content path. The Copilot desktop app can also use open tabs in its built-in browser as page context (MC1552386, rolling out November 2026); that is governed by whether the built-in browser is enabled, not by the web search policy.
Users also have a Web content toggle where the admin allows it, and Analyst and Cowork have no user toggle; test each Copilot surface you allow instead of assuming one behaviour.
done_when: The 'Allow web search in Copilot' policy is set to the value you chose, in the Cloud Policy service, and assigned to the right groups.
The decision (and any DLP rule for sensitive prompts) is documented and has been shared with users.

troubleshooting.symptom: Users still get web-grounded answers after you disabled the policy
troubleshooting.cause: Cloud Policy settings take time to reach clients, or the user is not in the group the policy is assigned to
troubleshooting.fix: Check the policy's group assignment in Cloud Policy, have the user restart the app, and re-test; confirm with audit whether a web search query was still logged.

troubleshooting.symptom: Security asks what was sent to Bing for a specific prompt
troubleshooting.cause: The generated query, not the prompt, is what leaves the service boundary
troubleshooting.fix: Search Purview audit / eDiscovery for the user's Copilot interaction and its logged web search query, as described in Microsoft's web search documentation.

troubleshooting.symptom: Copilot summarises an internal page even though web search is off
troubleshooting.cause: The page was open in the Copilot desktop app's built-in browser and used as page context
troubleshooting.fix: Decide separately whether the built-in browser should be enabled; see the related news item on open-tab page context.

rollback: Set 'Allow web search in Copilot' back to the previous value in Cloud Policy (keep the policy object so the change is auditable), and record why.
If a DLP rule for sensitive prompts caused false positives, switch it to simulation/audit mode rather than deleting it.

history.note: Added a verification step via web search query logging, pitfalls on other outside-content paths (desktop app open-tab context, user toggles), troubleshooting and rollback.
